passage: The skate park in Auckland was nearly empty when Kaito sat down on the ramp beside his friend Paulo and said, without looking up, "I've been hurting myself. Don't tell anyone. Promise." Paulo's stomach dropped, but he kept his voice steady. "Thanks for telling me. That took guts." He listened while Kaito talked about the pressure at home and the nights he couldn't sleep. Then Paulo said, "I can't promise to keep this secret, because I care whether you're safe. Are you safe right now?" Kaito said he wasn't planning anything tonight, but he was tired of everything. Paulo didn't leave him. They walked together to Paulo's house, where Paulo's dad switched off the TV, listened, and told Kaito it wasn't his fault he was struggling. With Kaito beside him, he phoned Kaito's mother and then a youth helpline that same evening.

qa.q: Where was Kaito sitting when he told Paulo?
qa.a: On the ramp at the nearly empty skate park.

qa.q: How did Paulo feel when Kaito spoke, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Paulo was shocked and scared; his stomach dropped, but he kept his voice steady.

qa.q: Which choice did Paulo make about the promise, and why?
qa.a: He said he couldn't keep it secret because Kaito's safety mattered, then stayed with Kaito and brought him to his dad instead of handling it alone.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Kaito when Paulo's dad switched off the TV and listened?
qa.a: Kaito may have felt taken seriously and less alone, especially hearing that it wasn't his fault he was struggling.

grounding: It shows a friend staying calm, thanking him for trusting, refusing a secrecy promise about safety, staying with him and bringing in a trusted adult and a helpline.

passage: Lights-out in the girls' hostel had come and gone when Pallavi whispered from the next bed, "Parul, I don't think I want to be here any more. Not just the hostel. Anywhere." Parul sat up. Her heart was thudding, but she switched on the small lamp and moved to sit beside her. "I'm really glad you told me. I'm listening." Pallavi cried and said she had been thinking about it all week, and that tonight felt worse. "Please don't tell Warden Ma'am." Parul held her hand. "I can't keep this one secret. You matter too much. I'm not leaving you." Without letting go, she pressed the intercom by the bed and asked the warden to come. The warden came within minutes, sat with both of them, and called the emergency number and Pallavi's parents. Parul stayed beside Pallavi until the ambulance team arrived, and walked with them to the gate.

qa.q: How did Parul call the warden?
qa.a: She pressed the intercom by the bed and asked the warden to come.

qa.q: What was Pallavi feeling that night, and what shows it?
qa.a: Pallavi felt hopeless and overwhelmed; she whispered that she didn't want to be anywhere, cried, and said tonight felt worse.

qa.q: Which choice by Parul kept Pallavi safest?
qa.a: Parul refused to keep it secret and never left Pallavi alone, calling the warden without letting go of her hand.

qa.q: How might the warden see Parul's call?
qa.a: The warden would likely see it as a brave, right choice, since it let adults get emergency help to Pallavi straight away.

grounding: It shows a teenager in the next hostel bed who listens calmly, will not keep a dangerous secret, never leaves Pallavi alone and gets emergency help through an adult.

passage:
Dear Hrithik,
I know you're angry with me. You asked me last night to keep it secret, and I didn't. I want to explain why.
When you told me in the park that you'd been hurting yourself, I was scared, but I tried to stay calm. I listened. I said thank you for trusting me, because I meant it. It took courage.
But I couldn't promise to keep it secret. Not when it's about your safety. That's why I didn't leave you, and why we called your mum from the bench together, and why she and I sat with you while you spoke to the helpline.
I'm not going anywhere. I'll come with you to the counsellor on Friday if you want.
Ishita

qa.q: Where did Hrithik tell Ishita?
qa.a: In the park.

qa.q: How did Ishita feel when Hrithik told her?
qa.a: Ishita felt scared but tried to stay calm, and was grateful that Hrithik trusted Ishita with it.

qa.q: What did Ishita do that was a wise response?
qa.a: Ishita stayed calm, listened, thanked Hrithik, refused to keep a safety secret, stayed with Hrithik and involved Hrithik's mum and a helpline that same night.

qa.q: How might Hrithik feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Hrithik may still feel angry but also cared for, understanding why Ishita couldn't keep it secret.

grounding: Shows a friend who stays calm, listens, thanks the person for trusting them, does not promise secrecy about safety and involves a trusted adult and helpline without leaving them alone.

passage: It was in the school washroom, between periods. I'm Neelam, and my best friend Salma pulled up her sleeve and showed me. She said, "Don't tell anyone. Promise." My whole body went cold. But I kept my voice quiet. I said, "Thank you for telling me. I know that was hard." I listened. She talked about feeling like she was drowning. Then I said the hardest thing: "I love you, and I can't keep this a secret, because it's about your safety. Let's go to Ms Shah together, right now." She was angry. She said I was betraying her. I didn't leave her. I walked with her to the counsellor's room and stayed while Ms Shah called her father. Weeks later Salma told me, "You did the right thing."

qa.q: Where did Salma show Neelam?
qa.a: In the school washroom, between periods.

qa.q: How did Neelam feel when Salma showed her?
qa.a: Neelam felt cold with fear but kept her voice quiet and calm.

qa.q: Why was refusing to promise secrecy the right choice?
qa.a: Because Salma's safety was at risk; Neelam went with her to the counsellor straight away, who called her father.

qa.q: How did Salma feel about Neelam's choice at first and later?
qa.a: At first Salma was angry and felt betrayed, but later she said Neelam did the right thing.

grounding: Shows a friend who stays calm, listens, thanks the person, refuses to keep a safety secret and brings in a trusted adult immediately without leaving her alone.

passage: I'm in Jyoti's class. I was there on the school trip when Mitali said it. We were in the dorm, and Mitali, crying, told Jyoti she was thinking of hurting herself that night. I don't know what Jyoti felt inside; her face stayed calm. She sat on the bed next to Mitali and said, "Thank you for telling me. I'm staying right here." Then she turned to me and said, "Aparna, please get Ms Rao. Now." I ran. Jyoti didn't leave Mitali's side for a second, not even when Mitali begged her to keep it secret. Jyoti said, "I can't. I care about you too much." Ms Rao came within minutes, called Mitali's parents and the helpline, and stayed with her all night.

qa.q: Who did Jyoti send Aparna to get?
qa.a: Ms Rao.

qa.q: How did Aparna seem to feel watching Jyoti respond?
qa.a: Aparna seemed tense and urgent, running at once, and impressed by how calm Jyoti stayed.

qa.q: What did Jyoti do that made her response safe and caring?
qa.a: She stayed calm and close, thanked Mitali, refused to promise secrecy, never left her alone and sent for a teacher immediately.

qa.q: How might Mitali have felt when Jyoti said "I care about you too much"?
qa.a: Mitali may have felt upset but also deeply cared for, even while begging for secrecy.

grounding: An observer describes a friend who stays calm, thanks the person, refuses to keep a safety secret, never leaves her alone and gets adult help immediately.

passage:
Monday. Behind the science block, Hansa rolled up her sleeve and showed Tenzin the marks. "I've been hurting myself. Don't tell anyone. Promise." Tenzin's heart thudded, but he kept his voice steady. "Thank you for trusting me. I'm so glad you told me. I can't promise to keep this secret, because I care about you being safe. Let's go to Ms Lhamo together, now." He walked beside her to the counsellor's room and waited outside. Ms Lhamo spoke with Hansa and called her mother that afternoon.
Wednesday. Hansa wouldn't look at him. "You told." Tenzin felt a flash of hurt, then answered calmly. "I didn't promise. I'd do it again."
The following Monday. Hansa sat beside him at lunch. "I've started seeing someone. My mum knows." She paused. "Thanks for not leaving me alone with it."

qa.q: Who did Tenzin walk Hansa to see on Monday?
qa.a: Ms Lhamo, the counsellor.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel when Hansa said "You told"?
qa.a: He felt a flash of hurt, but stayed calm and sure he had done the right thing.

qa.q: Which of Tenzin's choices was wise, and why?
qa.a: He stayed calm, thanked her, refused to promise secrecy about her safety and took her to a trusted adult straight away, so she wasn't left alone with it.

qa.q: How does Hansa see Tenzin by the following Monday?
qa.a: Her anger has turned to gratitude and trust; she thanks him for not leaving her alone with it.

grounding: Tenzin stays calm when a friend discloses self-harm, thanks her, doesn't promise secrecy about safety and takes her to a trusted adult right away.
